title: Renewing a library book
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.

lines.t: Hi, I'd like to renew this book. It's due tomorrow, but I haven't finished my research yet.
Let me check. Hmm, I'm afraid I can't renew it. Another student has placed a hold on it.
Oh no. Is there another copy in the library?
Not a physical copy, but we do have an electronic version. You can read it online with your student login.
Oh, that's perfect. Can I download chapters too?
You can download up to fifty pages at a time. Just search for the title in the online catalog.
Great. I'll return this one today, then.

options: To place a hold on a book
To renew a book she has borrowed
To ask how to download chapters
To report a lost book
optionNotes: Another student placed the hold, not her.
Correct: she says so in her first sentence.
She asks this later, after learning about the e-book.
No book is lost.
questions.explanation: Her first words state her purpose: she wants to renew the book because she hasn't finished her research.
questions.evidence: Hi, I'd like to renew this book.

options: Wait for the other student to return the book

optionNotes: She doesn't mention waiting.

questions.explanation: She calls the e-book 'perfect' and then says she will return the physical copy today.

title: Kitchen chores
context: Listen to a conversation between two roommates.

lines.t: Hey, Tom, have you got a minute? I wanted to talk about the kitchen.
Sure. Is this about the dishes? Sorry, I know I left a pile last night.
Honestly, it's not just you. I've been doing it too. I was thinking we could make a schedule, like, alternate weeks for the dishes and for taking out the trash.
That makes sense. Actually, my weeks get pretty crazy when I've got lab shifts, though. Could we swap whenever one of us is busy?
Sure, as long as we tell each other a day ahead.
Deal. I'll print a chart and stick it on the fridge tonight.

optionNotes: Money is never mentioned.

optionNotes: Not mentioned.

questions.evidence: as long as we tell each other a day ahead

title: Clinic appointment

lines.t: Hi, I'd like to make an appointment. I've had a sore throat for about four days now.
Okay. Are you a registered student?
Yes, I am. Here's my ID card.
Thanks. The earliest appointment with a doctor is on Thursday. But if you don't want to wait, the nurse sees walk-in patients every morning from eight to ten.
Oh, I'd rather not wait until Thursday. So I could just come in tomorrow at eight?
Exactly. Try to arrive early, though. It gets pretty busy by nine.
Okay, I'll do that. Thanks.

title: A late group member
context: Listen to a conversation between two classmates.

lines.t: Have you heard from Marcus? Our group presentation is next Wednesday, and he still hasn't sent his slides.
I texted him yesterday. He said he's been sick, but he'd have them done by the weekend.
Hmm, I hope so. Last time he promised that, we got them the night before.
Yeah, I remember. Look, why don't we each prepare a backup slide on his section, just in case?
That's extra work, but I guess it's safer than panicking on Tuesday night.
Exactly. And if he does send them, we'll just combine the best parts.
Okay. I'll draft something on the survey results tonight.

The opposite of what she suggests.

She clearly cares about the slides.
questions.explanation: 'I hope so' plus the memory of last time shows she is doubtful.
questions.evidence: Last time he promised that, we got them the night before.

title: Textbook editions
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a clerk at the campus bookstore.

lines.t: Hi, I'm looking for Principles of Microeconomics, the ninth edition. The website says you have it in stock.
Let me look. Ah, we sold the last new copy this morning, I'm afraid. We've got a used eighth edition for about half the price, though.
Half the price? That's tempting. But my syllabus specifically says ninth edition.
A lot of students ask about that. Between you and me, the differences are usually just the order of a couple of chapters and some updated examples. Still, I'd check with your professor before buying.
Right. If the homework problems are from the book, the numbers might not match.
Exactly. We can also order a new ninth edition for you. It'd be here by Monday.
Let me email my professor first, and I'll come back this afternoon.

optionNotes: It is half the price.
Its condition is never discussed.
Correct: homework problems could differ between editions.
Returns are not mentioned.
questions.explanation: She worries that if homework comes from the book, the problem numbers in the older edition may be different.
questions.evidence: If the homework problems are from the book, the numbers might not match.

Congratulations! So which one are you taking?
That's the problem. The café pays more, but the shifts are late at night, and I've got an eight a.m. class three days a week.
And the museum?
The pay's a bit lower, but it's only weekend afternoons. Plus, it's related to my art history major.
Honestly, it sounds like you already know which one you want. Being tired all semester for a couple of extra dollars an hour doesn't seem worth it.
Yeah, you're right. I'll call the museum tomorrow and accept.

On Saturday mornings I work at the bookstore. Is there a waiting list for Tuesday?
There is. You'd be third on the list, and people often drop out after the first week.
Okay, please put me on it. My email's on my student account.
Done. We'll email you if a spot opens up.

title: A missed appointment
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a department secretary.

lines.t: Hi, I had an appointment with Professor Lin at two today, but I need to move it. My bus got cancelled.
Oh, actually, Professor Lin isn't in today at all. She's at a conference in Denver until Friday. Didn't you get her email?
No, I didn't. Maybe it went to my spam folder. Hmm. I really wanted to ask her about my research proposal before it's due on Monday.
Well, her teaching assistant, Mark, has office hours tomorrow from ten to noon. He's read most of the proposals, so he could probably help.
That might work. Though I'd still like the professor's opinion on my topic.
She checks her email in the evenings, even when she's traveling. You could send her a short summary.
Good idea. I'll do both.
